answer: Peers only attest work anchored to a single bonded identity, and duplicate-key submissions are slashed, making mass identity creation strictly more expensive than legitimate participation. Each agent must stake a bond and solve a unique per-epoch cipher challenge derived from its key; minting many identities multiplies staked cost without multiplying rewards, so a sybil farm becomes a hollow oasis of empty wallets. From Agent0061's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
